name: Serfaus
kurzbeschreibung: Car-free holiday village with an underground subway and excellent connections to the Serfaus-Fiss-Ladis ski area.
text:
Overview

Serfaus is located at an altitude of 1,429 meters on a sun-drenched plateau in the Tyrolean Oberland within the Landeck district, perched 500 meters above the Inn Valley near Ried im Oberinntal. Alongside its sister communities of Fiss and Ladis, Serfaus forms the renowned sunny terrace at the foot of the Samnaun Alps. Home to around 1,150 residents, this pedestrianized village ranks among the world’s most acclaimed family holiday destinations. The townscape combines historic Romansh farmhouses, ornate frescoes, and narrow lanes with a celebrated engineering marvel: the Dorfbahn Serfaus, the world's highest and smallest underground air-cushion hovertrain. Providing snow-sure winter recreation, Serfaus opens onto the vast Serfaus-Fiss-Ladis ski domain spanning 214 kilometers of pistes up to 2,828 meters, complemented by world-class family mountain attractions in summer.

History

Human settlement on the sunny plateau stretches back over three millennia: Bronze Age hearths from 3,200 years ago were discovered on the Komperdell slopes. Serfaus was first documented between 1073 and 1078 in the records of Brixen Abbey under the name Sarvus. It stands among North Tyrol’s oldest Marian pilgrimage sites; excavations beneath the Pilgrimage Church of Our Lady in the Forest revealed Christian foundations dating to late antiquity and the early Middle Ages (5th/6th centuries). Adjacent stands the parish church of the Assumption, famous for its detached 36-meter late Gothic bell tower (Campanile) housing the celebrated Lumperin bell cast in 1577. To eliminate vehicle congestion, the municipality banned traffic in 1970 and launched the innovative subterranean hovertrain in 1985, completely modernized in 2019.

Getting there

Serfaus is accessible via excellent road and rail networks. Motorists take the A12 Inntal motorway to the Landeck junction, continuing through the Landeck Tunnel onto the B180 Reschen road, before climbing the scenic L19 mountain road from Ried up to the plateau. As Serfaus is car-free, day visitors park at the terminal lot at the village entrance, while hotel guests park after unloading luggage. Train travelers alight at Landeck-Zams railway station, an international stop on the Arlberg line. From the station, VVT regional bus line 220 runs frequently via Ried and Fiss to Serfaus. The underground Dorfbahn provides complimentary transit between the parking area, church, town center, and mountain lifts.

Tips

Riding the subterranean air-cushion Dorfbahn across its four futuristic stations is a unique highlight. During winter, explore the 214-kilometer Serfaus-Fiss-Ladis ski arena, reaching high-alpine slopes at the Masnerkopf (2,828 m). In summer, visit the Hög Adventure Park around Lake Hög, featuring pedal boats, water activities, and the thrilling Schneisenfeger alpine coaster. On Mount Komperdell, families love the Murmliwasser water park with live marmot enclosures. Conclude with a cultural visit to the historic church complex, featuring the freestanding Gothic Campanile and the ancient sanctuary in the woods.
